definition: a plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim, especially in business or competition
meaningKo: 전략, 장기적 목표를 달성하기 위한 계획
etymology: Greek 'strategia' meaning 'generalship, art of war' from 'strategos' (general)
contextSentence: A strategy is an integrative set of choices that positions you on a playing field of your choice in a way that you win.

definition: combining two or more things to form an effective unit or system
etymology: Latin 'integrare' meaning 'to make whole' from 'integer' (whole, complete)
contextSentence: A strategy is an integrative set of choices that positions you on a playing field of your choice in a way that you win.

definition: logical and consistent; forming a unified whole
etymology: Latin 'cohaerere' meaning 'to stick together' from 'co-' (together) + 'haerere' (to stick)
contextSentence: That theory has to be coherent.

definition: a detailed description of the design and materials used to make something; a clear statement of requirements
etymology: Latin 'specificare' meaning 'to mention particularly' from 'species' (kind) + 'facere' (to make)
contextSentence: There tends to be a list that has no internal coherence to it and no specification of a way that that is going to accomplish collectively some goal for the company.

definition: as a group; all together
etymology: Latin 'collectivus' from 'colligere' meaning 'to gather together'
contextSentence: No specification of a way that that is going to accomplish collectively some goal for the company.

definition: giving a feeling of ease, consolation, or reassurance
etymology: Latin 'confortare' meaning 'to strengthen greatly' from 'con-' (together) + 'fortis' (strong)
contextSentence: Planning is quite comforting.

definition: relating to or characterized by competition; having a strong desire to win
etymology: Latin 'competere' meaning 'to strive together' from 'com-' (together) + 'petere' (to seek)
contextSentence: A strategy, on the other hand, specifies an outcome, a competitive outcome that you wish to achieve.

definition: the degree to which a business or activity yields profit or financial gain
meaningKo: 수익성, 이윤을 낼 수 있는 정도
etymology: Latin 'profectus' meaning 'advance, progress' from 'proficere' (to accomplish)
contextSentence: Which involves customers wanting your product or service enough that they will buy enough of it to make the profitability that you'd like to make.

definition: a formal promise or assurance that certain conditions will be fulfilled
etymology: Old French 'garantie' from 'garant' meaning 'protector, defender'
contextSentence: We can't guarantee it.

definition: a person or thing acting or serving in place of another
etymology: Latin 'substituere' meaning 'to put in place of' from 'sub-' (under) + 'statuere' (to set up)
contextSentence: What they wanted to be is a substitute for Greyhound.

definition: to a very great degree; extremely; remarkably
etymology: Latin 'extraordinarius' from 'extra ordinem' meaning 'outside the normal order'
contextSentence: A way more convenient way to get around at a price that wasn't extraordinarily much greater than a Greyhound bus.

definition: to concentrate on and become expert in a particular subject or skill
etymology: Latin 'specialis' meaning 'particular, individual' from 'species' (kind, appearance)
contextSentence: We're not going to offer meals on the flights because we're going to specialize in short flights.

definition: to a great or significant extent; considerably
etymology: Latin 'substantialis' from 'substantia' meaning 'being, essence' from 'sub-' (under) + 'stare' (to stand)
contextSentence: So their strategy ended up being having a substantially lower cost than any of the major carriers.

definition: a company that transports goods or people, especially an airline
etymology: Anglo-French 'carier' meaning 'to transport in a vehicle' from Latin 'carrus' (wagon)
contextSentence: The major carriers were not trying to win against one another.

definition: to take part in an activity or event
etymology: Latin 'participare' meaning 'to share in' from 'pars' (part) + 'capere' (to take)
contextSentence: They were playing to participate, maybe buy more planes, get more gates.

definition: each of the parts into which something is divided; a portion of a market
etymology: Latin 'segmentum' meaning 'a strip cut off' from 'secare' (to cut)
contextSentence: Here's a way to be better than everybody else for this segment.

definition: a feeling of deep anxiety or dread, typically about the human condition or state of the world
etymology: German 'Angst' meaning 'fear, anxiety,' related to Latin 'angustia' (tightness, distress)
contextSentence: The most important thing to recognize is that strategy will have angst associated with it.

definition: a hope or ambition of achieving something; a strong desire to reach a goal
etymology: Latin 'aspirare' meaning 'to breathe upon, seek to reach' from 'ad-' (to) + 'spirare' (to breathe)
contextSentence: And that's why it's going to achieve this goal, this aspiration that we have.

definition: to make small adjustments to improve or fine-tune something
etymology: Old English 'twiccian' meaning 'to pluck, pull sharply'
contextSentence: What you want to have is a mechanism for tweaking it, toning it, and refining it so it gets better and better as you go along.

definition: a system of parts working together; a process or technique for achieving a result
etymology: Greek 'mēkhanē' meaning 'machine, device, contrivance'
contextSentence: What you want to have is a mechanism for tweaking it, toning it, and refining it.
